newsitem.title: USA: US House Democrat budget chief optimistic for deal.
newsitem.headline: US House Democrat budget chief optimistic for deal.

text.p: The chief Democrat on the House budget committee, Rep. John Spratt, said Thursday he is optimistic there will be a bipartisan agreement this year to balance the budget by the year 2002.
Speaking at the Brookings Institution, Spratt said the favorable economic climate and past spending reductions have contributed to create a good opportunity for a budget deal.

Spratt of South Carolina said he expected Republicans would fall two to three votes short and fail to pass in the House a Constitutional amendment to require a balanced budget. However, he said this would not get in the way of reaching a separate, bipartisan deficit-reduction package.
Tax cuts proposed by President Clinton and Republicans could complicate the process unless they are fully paid for by reducing tax breaks already in law, he said.

"After years of rising frustration ... something significant is finally happening ... I'm optimistic we will do it this year. We are closer to the goal than we've ever been in 15 years," he told the Brookings audience.

Although he has not seen Clinton's final tax proposal, Spratt said Clinton's past statements would indicate a potential for $120-130 billion worth of tax cuts. If Republicans add on a state tax cut release and a 50 percent capital gains tax rate reduction, the tax cut price tag would rise to $150-160 billion over the five years, he said.
Spratt added he doubted Congress would directly address changes in the Consumer Price Index formula, but for political reasons would prefer to allow the Labor Department to handle the issue.
